transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-07
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jared Lewis (Maple CTO), Maya Ortiz (Maple SRE Lead), Lynn Park (Product), Omar Ruiz (Security), Speaker 6

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): post launch checkin, some morning spikes, considering dedicated capacity, need SOC2 details and KPI for rollout.

00:00 Alex Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'll hand over to priya for a quick infra snapshot then we'll go through usage, latency, and next steps.
00:18 Priya Nair: thanks Alex. hi team, yeah so quick note — we pulled metrics from the last 30 days; average tokens/day 12.4M, peak prefix tokens about 2.2M across the 08:00-10:00 window, and KV-cache hit looked good, about 62% on your summarization pipeline, but we did see 99p spikes up to 1.1s for short-chat flows during the morning surge.
00:45 Maya Ortiz: uh that's the one i've been watching — not huge but user-visible; when our mobile app opens it funnels a lot of small requests, and the batching has some warmup mismatch so the 99p jumps.
01:05 Jared Lewis: yeah, to add context, we rounded out the pilot on december 28th and rolled into low-volume production jan 2nd. our main concern is that cost is creeping up, and we also have a product deadline mid-february for a wider rollout.
01:22 Alex Chen: totally. two levers we usually talk about: dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) which smooths latency and reduces per-token cost at scale, and hosted with smart routing + autoscale which is lower commitment but can get higher unit cost with bursts.
01:40 Lynn Park: can you give a rough delta today? like what are we paying per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated commit?
01:50 Priya Nair: rough ballpark — hosted for your current mix is about $10–13 per 1k tokens effective after embeddings and batching, dedicated commit can drop that to roughly $6–8 per 1k depending on commit length and quantization profile. numbers will change after we right-size batching and enable prefix cache more aggressively.
02:16 Omar Ruiz: quick security thing — we need to understand where audit logs live. do we get per-request logs when using hosted? also KMS support for customer-managed keys is critical.
02:28 Alex Chen: yes we can provide redwood-hosted audit logs with timestamped request traces at token level for enterprise plans; for private deployments we support BYOK via KMS/HSM. we'll send the SOC2 and audit log export samples after this call.
02:45 Maya Ortiz: earlier you mentioned KV cache hit is 62% — is that measured across all sessions or only long-lived chat? we think most of our traffic is single-shot summarization, so cache effectiveness might be overstated.
03:00 Priya Nair: good catch — that 62% was aggregated; for single-shot summarization it's closer to 18–22%. that explains some of the morning spikes since small single-shot requests can't benefit as much from prefix caching.
03:20 Jared Lewis: so what's the immediate recommendation — do we buy dedicated capacity or tune hosted? we have limited procurement cycles and prefer to avoid big commitments if possible.
03:31 Alex Chen: short answer: maybe a hybrid. start with a modest dedicated reserve to cover baseline 60–70% of steady throughput to get predictable latency and big cost savings, leave burst traffic on hosted with routing policies. that prevents over-commit while still getting SLO improvements.
03:49 Lynn Park: what's the lead time for dedicated pools?
03:52 Priya Nair: typically 2–4 weeks to provision and test in Dedicated if we're doing reserved hardware in the region you want. private/VPC can take longer depending on networking approvals.
04:06 Maya Ortiz: on the latency spike, you mentioned warmup mismatch — is that something fixed server-side or do we need to change client behavior (like persistent connections or larger batching)?
04:18 Priya Nair: both. we can tune server-side continuous batching policy and kernel selection for short sequences, but client-side persistent connections and micro-batching (small delay to allow batching) can drastically reduce 99p. worth testing both.
04:35 Jared Lewis: micro-batching sounds risky for our UX — some flows must be sub-200ms for perceived interactivity.
04:41 Alex Chen: agreed, micro-batching isn't for all flows. for the mobile startup funnel where a 300–400ms increase is acceptable, it's fine; for chat-like interactions you keep low-latency paths (dedicated smallest batch, hotter kernels). We'll map flows to routes.
05:00 Speaker 6: (inaudible)
05:10 Maya Ortiz: another operational ask — we'd like per-route cost breakdowns so product can attribute spend to features. does your console show token-level cost per route?
05:20 Priya Nair: yes Redwood Console has per-route and per-model token breakdowns, plus token-level cost and latency percentiles. we can export CSVs and hook to your internal billing dashboard.
05:38 Lynn Park: that would help with the mid-feb rollout business case.
05:44 Alex Chen: quick question on compliance from Omar. Omar, is SOC2 enough or do you need anything else like ISO/PCI?
05:51 Omar Ruiz: SOC2 is baseline. also want retention and deletion policies for PHI-ish data — we're not storing full PHI in the model, but we need proof of encryption at rest and in transit, access logs, and KMS BYOK for some endpoints.
06:06 Alex Chen: we can provide encryption at rest + transit; KMS BYOK is available for private deployments and for Certain enterprise-hosted tiers. we'll include the specifics in the security packet.
06:18 Maya Ortiz: about the morning surge — could a temporary autoremove of less important background tasks help? we already throttle analytics around 08:00 in some regions.
06:26 Jared Lewis: yes we can deprioritize non-customer-facing batch jobs, but the mobile surge is customer-facing.
06:32 Priya Nair: operational suggestion: route mobile startup funnel to a 'latency-first' route on dedicated baseline, route background and analytics to a 'cost-first' route in hosted. Redwood's smart routing can failover if dedicated capacity is saturated.
06:49 Lynn Park: timeline wise, what's our pilot-to-prod checklist?
06:53 Alex Chen: high level: (1) finalize committed capacity sizing, (2) run 99p latency benchmark with your production-like sample, (3) validate security scope and audit log formats, (4) smoke test canary rollout, (5) sign off on SLOs.
07:11 Priya Nair: for the benchmark we prefer a 2–4 hour window that includes warmup, steady state, and surge simulation. we'll need a 1GB anonymized sample or replay trace from you.
07:25 Lynn Park: we can extract a replay trace from our staging logs — lynn@maplehealth — i'll share by monday.
07:32 Jared Lewis: procurement question — if we commit to a 12-month dedicated pool, do we get penalty-free scaling adjustments? our volume may grow quickly.
07:41 Alex Chen: there's flexibility — commits are structured with headroom policies and burst capacity. we can architect a step-up cadence at pre-agreed thresholds to avoid penalties. i'll include sample clause language in the pricing sheet.
07:56 Maya Ortiz: any competitor differences we should be aware of? Anthropic said they'd do a hybrid private-hosted approach, but we're mainly comparing per-token economics and observability.
08:07 Priya Nair: competitive note: Anthropic offerings may have different kernel optimizations and fewer quantization profiles; we focus on model-aware quantization and cache-friendly serving which can give lower per-token costs for summarization-heavy workloads.
08:25 Speaker 6: (background)
08:40 Alex Chen: ok quick recap — action items as we captured: alex will send detailed capacity/pricing; priya will run benchmark once we get the replay trace; omar will send security checklist; lynn will provide traffic examples; maples to decide on pilot conversion and rollout window.
09:00 Lynn Park: sounds good. two small asks: can you include an estimated break-even point for dedicated commit in the spreadsheet, and please show a 6/12/24 month comparison?
09:12 Alex Chen: yep will include 6/12/24 month break-even and sensitivity scenarios.
09:18 Maya Ortiz: and can we schedule the infra deep dive for the week of jan 12th?
09:24 Priya Nair: i'm available jan 13/14 for a 90-min slot; i'll send a calendar invite after this call.
09:34 Jared Lewis: thanks everyone, appreciate the pragmatic approach.
09:38 Alex Chen: thanks team — we'll follow up in the next 48 hours with the security packet and pricing sheet.
09:46 Meeting end

Notes about transcription quality: speaker labels are mostly correct but there are short gaps and some background noise. references to product internals (KV-cache, quantization profiles, Dedicated) may be slightly garbled (e.g., "redwood dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated").
